requirement: During repository validation, Habeas MUST parse every first-party Rust source file in the project: every `.rs` file except those under `.git` or `target` directories at any depth or under the project-root `book`, `evidence`, or `vendor` directories. Every explicitly declared function or method, including trait methods and test helpers, and every struct, enum, and union MUST have a valid `{impl}`, `{cite}`, or `{test}` reference to a defined requirement or named example in a Rust comment attached to it or within its body. Comments belong to items under {cite}`requirements.references.outline_comments`; a comment before a field, variant, or attribute inside an item belongs to that item. A named example MUST reference a requirement under {cite}`requirements.examples.definition`. A reference in a string literal, on an enclosing module or impl block, or only in an evidence input MUST NOT count for the items it encloses. Habeas MUST report every unreferenced item with its file, line, kind, and name, and MUST report a Rust parse failure instead of silently skipping the file.
rationale:
## Verdict

The implementation meets every obligation in the requirement and is marked as `{impl}`. The tests cover the main points of the design space, including the failure cases. I found no acknowledged gaps (no FIXME) and no unmarked or unspecified behavior.

## Implementation

**File discovery**
- `rust_files` in `src/rust_coverage.rs` walks the project from the root.
- It skips `.git` and `target` directories at any depth.
- It skips `book`, `evidence` and `vendor` only when the directory's parent is the root.
- It collects every other `.rs` file, and it records directory and entry errors instead of skipping silently.

**Parsing and parse failures**
- `validate_rust_functions` reads each file and parses it through `missing_function_references`, which calls `outline::parse_with(&RUST_PROFILE, …)`.
- A read or parse failure is pushed to both `errors` and `discovery_errors` as `file:line: cannot parse Rust source: …`.

**Item kinds checked**
- The Rust profile in `src/outline/rust.rs` maps `function_item` and `function_signature_item` (trait methods and extern declarations) to `fn`.
- It maps `struct_item`, `enum_item` and `union_item` to `struct`, `enum` and `union`.
- `missing_function_references` checks exactly those four kinds, so functions, methods, trait methods, test helpers, structs, enums and unions are all covered.
- Items nested inside function bodies appear in the outline and are checked.

**Comment ownership**
- `assign_comments`, `run_owner` and `trailing_owner` in `src/outline/mod.rs` implement `requirements.references.outline_comments`.
- Comment runs are formed from consecutive lines, and a trailing comment forms its own run owned by the innermost node on its line.
- Other runs belong to the next sibling node, or to the container if none follows.
- Inner doc comments bind to their container.
- Comments inside an attached attribute are recorded for the attached item.
- Comments come from the tree-sitter grammar, so a reference in a string literal can never count.
- The code checks only comments owned by the item itself. A reference on an enclosing `mod` or `impl` therefore does not count for the items inside it.
- Evidence inputs are never consulted.

**What counts as a valid reference**
- A comment counts if `reference_roles` finds a non-term reference to a defined name.
- The name must be a requirement, or an example for which `example_references_requirement` in `src/evidence.rs` is true.
- That function requires a `{cite}` or `{test}` of a requirement, which matches `requirements.examples.definition`.
- Term references and unknown names do not count.

**Reporting**
- Each unreferenced item is reported as `file:line: kind name has no requirement or example citation`.
- The line is the declaration line, so file, line, kind and name are all present.
- `inspect_repository_with_progress` in `src/evidence.rs` calls `validate_rust_functions`.
- The `{impl}` markers on `missing_function_references`, `rust_files`, `validate_rust_functions`, `display_path`, `example_references_requirement`, `OutlineNode::display_name` and the call site are present. The extra `{impl}` markers on `validate_rust_functions` and the call site (`authoring.progress`, `authoring.batch`) correspond to other definitions.

## Tests

The unit tests are in `src/rust_coverage.rs`.

- **`finds_uncited_functions_without_using_enclosing_or_string_references`** covers these cases:
  - enclosing `mod`/`impl` references and references in string literals (normal and raw) do not count;
  - an unknown requirement name does not count;
  - a comment inside a body counts;
  - a comment run across a blank line counts;
  - a trailing comment belongs to the same-line item, not the next one;
  - an inner doc comment does not count for the next item;
  - an outer doc comment counts.
- **`checks_trait_test_helper_and_nested_functions_separately`** covers trait methods, nested functions, `{test}` references, test-helper functions, and a `{test}` of a named example.
- **`an_example_counts_only_when_it_references_a_requirement`** covers:
  - an example that cites a requirement;
  - an example that tests a requirement;
  - an orphan example;
  - an example that cites only another example;
  - an example that cites only a term;
  - an `{impl}` of a term.
- **`structs_enums_and_unions_need_references_attached_or_inside`** covers:
  - a reference attached before the attributes;
  - a reference inside the item before a field attribute;
  - a reference before an enum variant;
  - missing references on a struct, enum and union (all reported), and a nested struct;
  - reporting of line, kind and name.
- **`locates_functions_after_unicode_text`** checks correct line numbers after non-ASCII text.
- **`reports_all_files_and_parse_failures`** covers:
  - several files scanned and a parse failure reported;
  - the root-only and any-depth directory exclusions, including `src/vendor` and `src/book` being scanned;
  - `target`, `.git`, `evidence` and nested `target` being skipped.
- **`definitions`** is the shared test helper; it has its own `{test}` reference.

Further tests check the integration:

- `tests/authoring_batch.rs::discovery_errors_fail_before_configuration_or_inference` checks that a Rust parse failure surfaces as `cannot parse Rust source`.
- `tests/commands.rs::status_preserves_repository_wide_rust_findings_in_every_form` checks that the per-item error with file, line, kind and name reaches the CLI output.
- `src/outline/tests.rs` extensively tests comment-ownership rules, including the Rust inner doc comment binding, which this requirement relies on.

Each documented profile defines which grammar nodes are comments; the Markdown
profile's comments are HTML comment blocks, so an inline HTML comment within a
paragraph is text of its section. In every supported language, comments on consecutive lines with no other source
between them MUST form one comment run. A comment that follows other source on
the same line, including another comment, MUST form a run by itself and MUST belong to the innermost outline node
containing that line. Any other run MUST belong to the next outline node that
starts after it within the smallest node containing it; when that container has
no such node, the run MUST belong to the container, which is the root node at top
level. A profile MAY bind a comment kind to its container
instead: such a run MUST belong to the smallest node containing it. The Rust
profile MUST bind inner doc comments (`//!`, `/*!`) to their container, so a
file-level inner doc comment belongs to the root node. A reference in a comment MUST count for the node its run belongs to under

An mdBook chapter MAY define an example with an opening fence of at least three colons immediately followed by `{example} <name>` and a closing colon-only fence of at least the opening length. The full name MUST use the same chapter-derived namespace and valid-name rules as `{req}`. The body MUST include all Markdown between the fences, excluding surrounding whitespace, and MUST describe a concrete case with expected behavior. An example MUST contain at least one valid `{cite}` or `{test}` reference to a requirement it illustrates; `{cite}` makes the requirement an input to the example's assessment, and `{test}` makes the example an input to the requirement's assessment, under {cite}`requirements.references.targets`. An example MAY use both. An example directive inside a fenced code block MUST remain literal.
